t.5.15.1: Then the moon, itself spotless and gleaming like a cluster of white lotuses, moved forth across the spotless sky, like a swan gliding over dark blue water.
t.5.15.2: As if rendering him the service of a minister, the Moon, of spotless radiance, attended upon the son of the Wind with his light and his cool rays.
t.5.15.3: Then he saw Sītā, whose face was like the full moon, weighed down as if by burdens of grief, like a boat sunk in the water by its loads.
t.5.15.4: Longing to see Vaidehī, Hanumān, the son of Māruta, beheld rākṣasīs of dreadful appearance stationed not far off.
t.5.15.5: He saw one with a single eye and one with a single ear, one whose ears served as her covering, one without ears, one with spike-like ears, and one whose nostrils breathed from the top of her head.
t.5.15.6: And one with a hugely oversized head, one with a long, thin neck, one with dishevelled hair, likewise one without any hair, and one wrapped in her own hair as in a blanket.
t.5.15.7: One whose ears and forehead drooped, whose belly and breasts hung low, with dangling lips, with lips sagging onto her chin, with a long face and long knees.
t.5.15.8: He saw a short one and a tall one, a hunchbacked one, a misshapen one and a dwarfish one, a fearsome one, one in twisted garments, one with tawny eyes, and one with a deformed face.
t.5.15.9: Deformed, tawny and dark, wrathful and fond of quarrels, they bore great spears of black iron, hammers and maces.
t.5.15.10: He saw some with the faces of boars, deer, tigers, buffaloes, goats and jackals, some with the feet of elephants, camels and horses, and others whose heads were sunk into their bodies.
t.5.15.12: Some had no noses, some had huge noses, some had crooked noses and some were noseless; some had noses like an elephant's trunk, and some had nostrils that breathed from their foreheads.
t.5.15.11: He saw some with one hand and one foot, and others with the ears of a donkey or the ears of a horse.
t.5.15.13: He saw them, some with elephants' feet, some with huge feet, some with cows' feet, some with tufts of hair on their feet, some with enormous heads and necks, and some with enormous breasts and bellies.
t.5.15.14: He saw them with enormous mouths and eyes, and likewise with long tongues and nails.
t.5.15.15: And he saw rākṣasīs of dreadful appearance, with the faces of horses, camels and donkeys, holding spears and clubs in their hands, wrathful and fond of quarrels.
t.5.15.17: The best of monkeys saw those women, their limbs smeared with flesh and blood, feeding on flesh and blood, a sight to make the hair stand on end.
t.5.15.16: Fearsome rākṣasīs with smoke-grey hair and misshapen faces, ceaselessly drinking liquor, ever fond of meat and wine.
t.5.15.18: He saw them seated around the great-trunked tree, encircling it, and beneath it that blameless lady, the daughter of a king.
t.5.15.19: The glorious Hanūmān beheld the daughter of Janaka, lustreless, tormented by grief, her hair matted with dirt.
t.5.15.21: Her, bereft of fine ornaments yet adorned by her devotion to her husband, held captive by the lord of the rākṣasas and parted from her kinsfolk.
t.5.15.20: He saw her like a star whose merit is exhausted, fallen from the sky and dropped down upon the earth: rich in the fame of her virtuous conduct, yet wretched, deprived of the sight of her husband.
t.5.15.22: She was like a she-elephant cut off from her herd, hemmed in by a lion and held captive, and like the crescent of the moon at the close of the rainy season, veiled by autumn clouds.
t.5.15.23: He saw Sītā, her form worn and wasted for want of her lord's touch, like a lute left unplayed; she was devoted to her husband's welfare, yet held, though so unfit for it, in the power of the rākṣasas.
t.5.15.25: Hanumān beheld the queen, like a creeper without flowers; her limbs were smeared with dirt, and yet she was adorned by her own beauty.
t.5.15.24: There in the midst of the Aśoka grove she was plunged into an ocean of grief and surrounded by those women, like Rohiṇī beset by a planet.
t.5.15.27: The monkey Hanumān saw her, the fawn-eyed goddess, closely surrounded, her face downcast with misery, yet undaunted by virtue of her husband's splendour.
t.5.15.26: Like a lotus stalk smeared with mud, she both shines and does not shine: the radiant lady clad in a soiled and worn-out garment.
t.5.15.28: Hanumān, seeing Sītā, the dark-eyed one guarded by her own virtue, that Sītā whose eyes were like those of a young fawn,
t.5.15.29: She was like a frightened young doe, glancing about on every side, and seemed almost to scorch with her sighs the trees bearing tender shoots.
t.5.15.30: Her, like a mass of sorrows gathered together, like a wave of grief risen high, emaciated, with finely proportioned limbs, beautiful even without ornaments.
t.5.15.31: Beholding Maithilī, Māruti obtained a joy beyond compare, and seeing her, the one with intoxicating eyes, he shed tears born of joy.
t.5.15.33: Thrilled at the sight of Sītā, Hanumān remained concealed.
t.5.15.32: There Hanumān let go and bowed in reverence to Rāghava; and the valiant one, having paid homage to Rāma and to Lakṣmaṇa,
